functions.name: discount_rate
functions.docstring: Members get 20%; other orders >= 100 get 10%; reject negative totals.

functions.name: order_total
functions.docstring: Compute discounted total, rounded to two decimal places.

cases.description: Member with a non-negative total below the 100 threshold receives the member rate, since the member branch takes precedence over the total-based branch.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize total values below 100 (e.g. 0, 50, 99.99) with member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.2 for every member order regardless of total magnitude.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: Non-member order with total at or above 100 receives the 10% volume discount.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize total values at/above 100 (e.g. 100, 250, 1000) with member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.1 for each qualifying non-member total.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: Non-member order below 100 receives no discount.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize non-negative totals strictly below 100 (e.g. 0, 1, 99) with member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.0 for each sub-threshold non-member total.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: Exact threshold total of 100 for a non-member hits the inclusive >= 100 branch and yields the 10% rate, while 99 just below yields 0.0.
cases.input_strategy: Call with total=100 and total=99, member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: 100 returns 0.1; 99 returns 0.0, confirming the inclusive boundary.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: Total of 0 is the lowest valid non-negative total and is accepted without error.
cases.input_strategy: Call with total=0, member=False and member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Non-member returns 0.0; member returns 0.2; no ValueError raised.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: A negative total is rejected with ValueError before any discount branching occurs, even for members.
cases.input_strategy: Call with negative totals (e.g. -0.01, -1, -100) and both member=False and member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises ValueError with message 'negative total' regardless of the member flag.
cases.setup: Import pytest and discount_rate from discount; use pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative total').

cases.description: Member flag takes priority over the total>=100 branch, so a member order of 100 still yields the 20% member rate rather than 10%.
cases.input_strategy: Call with total=100 and above (e.g. 100, 500) with member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.2, demonstrating member precedence over the volume discount branch.
cases.setup: Import discount_rate from discount.

cases.description: Non-numeric totals cause a TypeError when compared to 0, documenting the unvalidated type contract.
cases.input_strategy: Call with total=None and total='abc' and total=[], member defaulting to False.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises TypeError because the < 0 comparison is unsupported for these types.
cases.setup: Import pytest and discount_rate from discount; use pytest.raises(TypeError).

cases.description: Item.subtotal multiplies price by quantity for a typical positive-price, positive-quantity item.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize representative (price, quantity) pairs with price > 0 and quantity > 1, e.g. (2.5, 4), (10.0, 3), (0.99, 100).
cases.expected_behavior: Returns price * quantity exactly as a float for each pair.
cases.setup: Import Item from models; construct Item(price=..., quantity=...) and call subtotal().

cases.description: Default quantity of 1 makes subtotal equal the price when quantity is omitted, covering the dataclass default.
cases.input_strategy: Construct Item(price=7.25) with quantity omitted; also compare with Item(price=7.25, quantity=1).
cases.expected_behavior: Both instances return 7.25, confirming the default quantity is 1.
cases.setup: Import Item from models; do not pass quantity.

cases.description: Zero price or zero quantity yields a zero subtotal and must not raise, since the guard checks strict negativity.
cases.input_strategy: Call with (price=0, quantity=5) and (price=10, quantity=0) and (price=0, quantity=0).
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.0 for each case with no ValueError.
cases.setup: Import Item from models; construct each instance and invoke subtotal().

cases.description: A negative price is rejected even when quantity is positive, testing the guard's price branch independently.
cases.input_strategy: Call with negative prices (e.g. -0.01, -5.0) and positive quantity 2.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises ValueError with message containing 'negative price or quantity'.
cases.setup: Import pytest and Item from models; wrap in pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative price or quantity').

cases.description: A negative quantity is rejected even when price is non-negative, testing the guard's quantity branch independently.
cases.input_strategy: Call with positive price 10.0 and negative quantities (e.g. -1, -100) including zero price with negative quantity.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises ValueError with message containing 'negative price or quantity' for every combination.
cases.setup: Import pytest and Item from models; wrap in pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative price or quantity').

cases.description: Both fields negative also raises the same ValueError before multiplication, confirming the combined guard short-circuits.
cases.input_strategy: Call with price=-3.0 and quantity=-2.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises ValueError rather than returning a positive product of two negatives.
cases.setup: Import pytest and Item from models; use pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative price or quantity').

cases.description: Non-numeric price or quantity causes a TypeError from the comparison, documenting the unvalidated type contract.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize invalid operands: price=None with quantity=1; price='abc' with quantity=1; price=1.0 with quantity='x'.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises TypeError from the '<' comparison for each invalid operand.
cases.setup: Import pytest and Item from models; wrap in pytest.raises(TypeError).

cases.description: An empty item list sums to 0, which is a valid non-negative total below the 100 threshold, so no discount applies and the function returns 0.0.
cases.input_strategy: Call order_total([]) with member defaulting to False.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 0.0 (0 * 1.0 rounded to two decimals).
cases.setup: Import order_total from order.

cases.description: Non-member order whose summed subtotals stay below 100 gets no discount, exercising the aggregate sum plus the no-discount rate path.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize item sets whose summed price*quantity is strictly below 100, e.g. [Item(10.0, 2)] (20), [Item(2.5, 4), Item(10.0, 3)] (40), [Item(0.99, 100)] (99).
cases.expected_behavior: Returns the raw summed total unchanged for each below-threshold non-member order.
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; construct each item list and call order_total(items, member=False).

cases.description: Non-member order with summed subtotal at or above 100 receives the 10% volume discount applied to the sum before rounding.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize item sets summing to >=100, e.g. [Item(50.0, 2)] (100), [Item(25.5, 4)] (102), [Item(100.0, 10)] (1000), with member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns sum * 0.9 rounded to two decimals (e.g. 100 -> 90.0, 102 -> 91.8).
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; construct each item list and call order_total(items, member=False).

cases.description: Member order receives the 20% member discount regardless of the summed total, including totals below the volume threshold.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize member item sets with various sums, e.g. [Item(10.0, 2)] (20), [Item(2.5, 4)] (10), [Item(60.0, 1)] (60), calling order_total(items, member=True).
cases.expected_behavior: Returns sum * 0.8 rounded to two decimals (e.g. 20 -> 16.0, 10 -> 8.0).
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; construct each item list and call order_total(items, member=True).

cases.description: Exact threshold sum of 100 for a non-member hits the inclusive >= 100 volume branch and yields the 10% discount, while a sum just below yields none.
cases.input_strategy: Call with [Item(50.0, 2)] (sum exactly 100) and [Item(49.99, 2)] (sum 99.98), member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Sum 100 returns 90.0; sum 99.98 returns 99.98, confirming the inclusive boundary on the aggregated total.
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; build each list and invoke order_total with member=False.

cases.description: Member flag takes precedence over the volume branch, so a member order with summed total >= 100 still receives the 20% member rate, not 10%.
cases.input_strategy: Call with item lists summing to >=100, e.g. [Item(50.0, 2)] (100) and [Item(100.0, 10)] (1000), member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns sum * 0.8 (100 -> 80.0, 1000 -> 800.0), demonstrating member precedence over the volume discount.
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; call order_total(items, member=True).

cases.description: Result rounding to two decimals is applied to the discounted product, covering values where the raw product has more than two decimal places.
cases.input_strategy: Call with [Item(12.345, 1)] (sum 12.345, non-member) and [Item(12.345, 1)] with member=True.
cases.expected_behavior: Non-member returns round(12.345, 2) == 12.35 (or the exact value from round's banker's rounding) and member returns round(9.876, 2) == 9.88, matching round(total * (1 - rate), 2).
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; construct the item and call with member False and True.

cases.description: Item.subtotal rejects negative price/quantity, so order_total propagates ValueError from the sum generator before any discount or rounding.
cases.input_strategy: Call with [Item(-1.0, 1)] and [Item(10.0, -2)] and [Item(5.0, 1), Item(-3.0, 2)], member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises ValueError with message containing 'negative price or quantity' for each list.
cases.setup: Import pytest, Item from models, and order_total from order; wrap in pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative price or quantity').

cases.description: When the aggregated total would be negative the discount dependency rejects it, documenting propagation of discount_rate's ValueError through order_total.
cases.input_strategy: This cannot be reached through valid Items (their guard forbids negative subtotals); verify the float aggregation path instead by using a duck-typed item whose subtotal returns a negative float, e.g. a stub with subtotal() -> -5.0.
cases.expected_behavior: order_total raises ValueError('negative total') propagated from discount_rate for the negative aggregate.
cases.setup: Import pytest, order_total from order; pass a list containing a stub object exposing subtotal() returning -5.0 (duck-typed like Item) and wrap in pytest.raises(ValueError, match='negative total').

cases.description: None or a non-iterable passed as items makes the sum() call fail before any discount logic runs.
cases.input_strategy: Call order_total(None) and order_total(42) with member defaulting to False.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises TypeError because None and int are not iterable for sum().
cases.setup: Import pytest and order_total from order; wrap in pytest.raises(TypeError).

cases.description: A list containing a non-Item lacking a callable subtotal attribute causes an AttributeError during aggregation.
cases.input_strategy: Call order_total([object()]) and order_total([1, 2]) with member defaulting to False.
cases.expected_behavior: Raises AttributeError because the objects expose no subtotal() method.
cases.setup: Import pytest and order_total from order; wrap in pytest.raises(AttributeError).

cases.description: order_total delegates the discount-decision total to discount.discount_rate, so the aggregated sum (not individual item prices) is what crosses the 100 threshold.
cases.input_strategy: Call with [Item(40.0, 1), Item(40.0, 1), Item(20.0, 1)] (three items each below 100, summed exactly 100), member=False.
cases.expected_behavior: Returns 90.0, showing the volume discount keys off the summed total rather than any single item subtotal.
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; call order_total(items, member=False).

cases.description: The member flag is passed straight through to discount_rate, so order_total's member argument must reach the discount dependency unchanged.
cases.input_strategy: Call the same list [Item(10.0, 1)] with member=False and member=True and compare results.
cases.expected_behavior: Non-member returns 10.0 and member returns 8.0, revealing that the member argument is forwarded to the discount computation.
cases.setup: Import Item from models and order_total from order; invoke both flag values.
